events.continuity_hook: Closes practical details for the Texas episode after the flight choice was made.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the trip sequence is bookable as planned and flag any hotel or car timing that needs a phone call before purchase.
events.scenario_brief: Tessa has ticketed the Austin-to-Salt Lake City return with the cleaner timing and is doing a last check on the Texas run before hotel checkout locks in. She needs the Dallas arrival hotel, two north Austin nights, rental-car pickup and return times, breakfast start times, and late-dinner options compared against the Fort Worth Monday meeting, the Waco and Temple Tuesday visits, and the Wednesday evening north Austin event. The only loose item is whether a newly offered Wednesday morning school visit near Round Rock can fit without moving hotels.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the next fall work-trip episode after the Texas arrangements are nearly set.
events.interaction_goal: Lay out the realistic route shapes, compare drive-time risk, and identify hotel zones that keep early starts simple.
events.scenario_brief: Tessa begins a late-October upper Midwest recruitment loop with a Monday counselor breakfast in Eden Prairie, a Monday evening fair in Saint Paul, Tuesday school visits near Rochester, a Wednesday transfer fair in La Crosse, and a Thursday morning high-school visit in Eau Claire. She needs to decide whether to fly Salt Lake City to Minneapolis-Saint Paul round trip and drive the loop, or use a smaller return airport after La Crosse to shorten the last drive. Hotel areas, rental-car timing, and a Thursday afternoon trip home are unresolved.

events.continuity_hook: Adjusts the upper Midwest loop once the two river-corridor event times firmed up.
events.interaction_goal: Recommend the lowest-stress overnight sequence and note which hotel areas have breakfast and nearby dinner options.

Tessa now needs the middle nights reworked so she is not doing a long late-night drive after the fair while still keeping the hotel count to four nights. The open choice is a La Crosse overnight after the fair versus driving partway toward Eau Claire before sleeping.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the upper Midwest loop from routing and hotel areas into airfare purchase details.
events.interaction_goal: Select the flight plan, summarize the rental-car return implication, and call out seat selection and receipt items for booking.

The Salt Lake City to Minneapolis-Saint Paul nonstop fits the arrival plan, but the best Thursday return after the Eau Claire visit is either a late-afternoon nonstop from Minneapolis-Saint Paul or a cheaper one-stop routing from a smaller airport with a tight connection. events.continuity_hook: Shifts from fall recruitment loops into a short professional conference trip.
events.interaction_goal: Compare a Monday-afternoon arrival against a Tuesday-morning arrival, and shortlist hotels that balance conference access, reimbursement fit, and meal logistics.
events.scenario_brief: Tessa starts planning a December admissions conference in Denver. The conference begins Tuesday at noon and ends Thursday mid-afternoon, with an optional Wednesday evening networking reception near the convention center. The official hotel block is convenient but over her nightly reimbursement cap and does not clearly include breakfast, while nearby practical hotels may require a short ride or light-rail hop. She has not decided whether to arrive Monday afternoon or Tuesday morning.

events.continuity_hook: Follows the initial Denver conference comparison after rates and room availability changed.
events.interaction_goal: Rank the three hotel choices for booking and identify the reimbursement question Tessa should clear before paying.
events.scenario_brief: The Denver conference block sent a rate notice with only one remaining room type, and the nearby hotel Tessa liked is now cheaper for two nights but farther from the Wednesday evening reception. She needs to choose between the block hotel, the cheaper breakfast-included option near a rail stop, and a third hotel within walking distance of the convention center but with fewer food choices. The unresolved detail is whether reimbursement will cover the block rate if the lower-priced rooms are gone.
